title: A structured decision template package for tumour boards: a pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster trial across a regional cancer network
abstract: Objective: to test whether a structured decision template with board coordinators and monthly feedback increases complete documentation of tumour board decisions, shortens time to first treatment and improves patients' understanding without lengthening meetings. Design: pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster trial across 11 boards in six hospitals, with the order of boards set by chance within size strata on the network's six-wave rollout in 2027. Results and conclusions will follow the trial.
introduction: Only about half of sampled tumour board discussions document every core decision item, and incomplete documentation is linked to delays and conflicting messages to patients. Structured templates and coordinators have been evaluated only in before-after or convenience-ordered studies.
methods: Twenty discussions per board per month are reviewed against seven items by reviewers from other hospitals; treatment dates and meeting times come from routine systems; patients complete a five-item understanding questionnaire. Analysis uses mixed-effects models with period effects and small-sample corrections. A parallel design first considered was superseded because it was underpowered and incompatible with the licensing schedule.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present completeness by period and exposure, time to first treatment, understanding scores, meeting duration and delivery measures.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the effect against secular trends, the data gap for four boards and the few clusters, and state what the network should keep.
limitations: Eleven clusters; unblinded delivery; possible secular trends; a two-month data gap for four boards.
conclusion: To be written after the trial; it will not claim effects on survival.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge cluster randomised trials, with TIDieR
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty.
